questions.q: According to the lesson, why can't automated metrics fully replace human review?
options: Automated metrics are always slower than human review
Some qualities like tone and real helpfulness are genuinely subjective, and human review catches failure modes nobody thought to write a rubric for yet
Automated metrics are illegal to use in production
Human reviewers are always more accurate on every type of question
questions.explain: The lesson explains that subjective qualities and unknown failure modes are where human review still adds value beyond automated grading.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend instead of reviewing every single output by hand?
options: Stop doing any human review at all
Only review outputs from one specific user
Sample a representative set, plus anything automated metrics flagged as borderline
Review outputs in a random order with no selection criteria
questions.explain: The lesson recommends sampling rather than reviewing everything, since full review collapses past a few dozen cases a week.

questions.q: Why does the lesson prefer a structured rubric with specific criteria over an open-ended '1 to 5' rating?
options: Structured rubrics take longer to use than open-ended ratings
Specific, checkable criteria produce ratings different reviewers actually agree on, while open-ended ratings produce noise
Open-ended ratings are more precise than structured rubrics
Structured rubrics can only be used by AI models, not humans
questions.explain: The lesson states that a rubric with specific criteria produces agreement between reviewers, while a holistic 1-5 score produces noise.

questions.q: If two careful reviewers disagree often on the same cases using the same rubric, what does the lesson say that signals?
options: That one of the reviewers should be replaced immediately
That the rubric itself is ambiguous and needs fixing, not the reviewers
That the AI system has a critical bug
That human evaluation should be abandoned entirely
questions.explain: The lesson states that frequent disagreement under inter-rater reliability checks means the rubric is ambiguous and needs to be fixed.

questions.q: What does the lesson say happens when human review has no feedback loop into the eval dataset or grading criteria?
options: It becomes a one-time check rather than an actual system
It automatically improves the model's accuracy
It becomes illegal to continue using
Nothing changes; feedback loops are unnecessary for human review
questions.explain: The lesson lists 'no feedback loop' as a pitfall, noting that review findings need to feed back into the dataset and grading criteria to form an actual system.
